# SK2064 — Use && or || rather than & or | on booleans

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `&` or `|` joins two `bool` operands whose right side has no side effect, so the non-short-circuiting operator evaluates a guard's right half that the guard exists to skip.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S2178 |

## Why

`if (node != null & node.Ready)` evaluates `node.Ready` whichever way the null check went, so the check protects nothing and the `NullReferenceException` it was written to prevent is thrown anyway. One character separates it from the code that works. ⚠ **The rule is semantic because the operand type decides everything.** `&` and `|` on integers and on `[Flags]` enums are the *only* way to write those operations, and reporting `flags & Mask` would be a catastrophe rather than a false positive; the rule therefore fires only where both operands are non-nullable `bool` and the operator is the language's own, never a user-defined one.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (node != null & node.Ready) { Use(node); }
```

Write:

```csharp
if (node != null && node.Ready) { Use(node); }

// and the two shapes that are never reported:
var masked = flags & FileAttributes.ReadOnly;   // integral and enum operands
if (ValidateName(x) & ValidateAge(x)) { }       // both sides must run, so & is deliberate
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Integral and enum operands are excluded, and nothing else in this rule matters as much.** `flags & Mask`, `a | b` on `int`, and every `[Flags]` combination are `&`/`|` used correctly and have no `&&` form at all; the rule reads the operand types and fires only where both are exactly non-nullable `System.Boolean`. ⚠ **`bool?` is excluded too, and it is not the same exclusion.** Lifted `&` and `|` on nullable booleans are three-valued — `null & false` is `false`, not `null` — and `&&`/`||` cannot express that, so the rewrite would change the answer rather than the evaluation order. A user-defined `operator &` or `operator |`, and any operand whose type did not resolve, are excluded for the same reason: the operator does not mean what the rule assumes. ⚠ **A right operand with a side effect is deliberate and is never reported.** An invocation, an assignment, an `await`, an `++`, an object creation or an element access on the right is the documented reason to reach for `&` — both validators must run so both messages are collected — and short-circuiting it would delete work. Only a right operand built from names, member-access paths, literals, `is`/`as` tests and comparisons over them is reported. ⚠ **A mixed bitwise expression is declined rather than reported**, because `&` and `|` bind tighter than `&&` and `||` and swapping one token inside `a | b & c` regroups the whole expression. If the node's parent, or either of its operands, is another `&`, `|` or `^`, the rule stays silent — an under-report in the one place where the fix could silently change the program. `^` is not examined at all: it has no short-circuiting form. The fix replaces the single operator token and nothing else, so it is safe to apply without review. Generated code is excluded.
